## p137 A4, p137 A5 — Surviving Transylvania situation report

**Related source pages:** [p128 B1](128.md#source-p128-b1), [p129 A7](129.md#source-p129-a7), [p129 A8](129.md#source-p129-a8).

<a id="edition-cases-military-transylvania-situation-report-surviving-transylvania-situation-report"></a>



Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

This is a proposed cross-page assembly of an eight-part message marked 1840 / 18.40, 8 TLE, LP v NKJ. Parts 1, 7 and 8 survive on pp128–129; p137 supplies part 4 and conditional partial readings of interference-damaged parts 5 and 6. Parts 2 and 3 remain unlocated. All uses of the Nov4–6 key retain its published square and ranks.

The headings conflict: pp128–129 say 5 November with different evening receipt times; p137 has a 6 November page heading and 08.14 on 5 November in its receipt line, alongside the 18.40 origin. Matching headers, part numbers and content support the association but do not resolve those dates or prove an exact transmission history.

The conditional complete reading orders the removal of economic and
administrative staffs before military movements begin:

**Readable German — conditional complete part-5 proposal:**

> Anschliessend muessen vor Beginn militaerischer Bewegungen Personal der
> Wirtschafts- und Verwaltungsstaebe ab 6. November abgeschoben werden.

The proposal reaches **126/126 positions**, including two separately priced
`X` separators after `WIRTSCHAFTS` and `WERDEN`. Each separator supplies one
missing coordinate while retaining its observed half. The full part costs
**seven observed substitutions, four printed-mask fills and 37 missing-coordinate
fills** under the earlier conditional 0/37 interference frame. The source-68
V alternative lowers the substitution total to six. The literal `MUESSEN`
and date label `6` are retained.

The [completion account](../../experiments/p137_governing_clause/README.md#completing-the-two-separators)
shows all 36 possible residual label pairs before the punctuation choice.
This completes the proposed reading of part 5; the missing parts and the

<a id="edition-cases-military-transylvania-situation-report-missing-and-unread-material"></a>

### Missing and unread material

The p128 copy explicitly states that parts 2–6 are missing. The separate p137 page supplies independent surviving material for 4–6. It does not restore parts 2/3, and part 6 has no stated length. A [separate conditional A6 edition](#edition-cases-military-p137-publicity-fragment) proposes 25 letters in a 254-slot frame, preserving 102 unknown positions and the equally compatible 256/258-slot alternatives. Its polarity and intervening verb remain unread.

<a id="edition-cases-military-transylvania-situation-report-evidence-and-totals"></a>

### Evidence and totals

The five readable physical sources provide 550 modeled plaintext positions: 499 fixed under their declared raw geometries and 530 after the stated candidates. Costs are six observed-coordinate substitutions, seven fills of printed dashes/invalid glyphs, and 24 missing-coordinate fills. The 74-slot part 6 now has its own [25-letter conditional catalogue entry](#edition-cases-military-p137-publicity-fragment); it remains excluded from these five-source totals. That separate model has zero raw fixed positions and does not establish the missing sentence.

The earlier corpus screen already recognized parts 1/7/8. Lasry et al. describe a different thirteen-part report of 3 November in their Table 3; this edition makes no first historical decipherment claim. A complete 788-block exact-window search found only one short 12-coordinate incidental lead and no missing part 2/3.

## p137 A6 — Conditional publicity word fragments with unresolved polarity and verb

**Edition context:** p137 A6 — Conditional publicity fragment in an interference-damaged report.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p137-publicity-fragment-p137-a6--conditional-publicity-fragment-in-an-interference-damaged-report"></a>



**Source review and conditional reconstruction: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**
The sixth part preserves 74 coordinate slots after an explicit interference
annotation. A language-guided proposal places `DER OEFFENTLICHKEIT` and
`BLEIBEN` in a conditional 254-slot frame. Its **25 proposed letters retain
15 observed halves and supply 35 absent halves**. None of the 71 received
valid coordinates is changed. These words are conditional proposals, not
cipher-only recoveries or a completed sentence.

<a id="source-p137-a6"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-p137-publicity-fragment-p137-a6"></a>

### p137 A6

**Readable German — conditional word fragments only; the intervening fourteen positions remain unresolved:**

> […] der Oeffentlichkeit […] bleiben […]

The central noun means “the public.” The excerpt does not establish whether
something was to remain hidden, become known, or remain available to the public.
Both the polarity and the intervening verb have materially different
zero-change alternatives. No event or policy is inferred from this fragment.

```text

```

</details>

Every plaintext position lacks at least one coordinate in this frame. The
received halves still constrain letter domains, but do not independently
fix even one complete letter pair.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

```text
?????????????DEROEFFENTLICHKEIT??????????????BLEIBEN???????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????
```

**102 plaintext positions remain unassigned**, including all fourteen positions

<a id="edition-cases-military-p137-publicity-fragment-exact-support-and-semantic-alternatives"></a>

### Exact support and semantic alternatives

All indices below are zero-based. A received half is a constraint on a letter,
not an independently fixed letter.

| Proposed word | Plaintext positions, inclusive | Observed halves retained | Added-slot fills | Wholly absent letters |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `DER` | 13–15 | 2 | 4 | 1 |
| `OEFFENTLICHKEIT` | 16–30 | 9 | 21 | 6 |
| `BLEIBEN` | 45–51 | 4 | 10 | 3 |
| **Primary proposal** | **25 positions** | **15** | **35** | **10** |

The ten wholly unobserved proposed letters are **15 R, 17 E, 19 F, 22 T,
25 C, 26 H, 29 I, 46 L, 49 B and 51 N**. Their two coordinates are both
supplied. The fifteen remaining proposed letters each retain exactly one
received half.

The discovery model suggested the fuller wording
`DEROEFFENTLICHKEITNICHTVERBORGENBLEIBEN`. Its apparent fluency does not resolve
two independent ambiguities:

| Unresolved span | Equal-price examples | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| 31–35 | `NICHT`, `IMMER`, `LANGE` | “Not,” “always” and “for a long time” differ materially. |
| 36–44 | `VERBORGEN`, `VERGOENNT` | “Hidden” and “granted/allowed” support different readings. |

All six combinations have **39 assigned letters, 23 observed halves and
55 added-slot fills**, with zero observed-coordinate changes. Each has
sixteen wholly unobserved letters. They are separately priced alternatives,
not equally established historical sentences. The primary output therefore
leaves both spans unread. Other local dictionary matches also exist;
this list does not exhaust all possible wording. Even `DER` and `BLEIBEN`
remain language-guided choices within their coordinate domains.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p137-publicity-fragment-conditional-length-and-neighboring-parts"></a>

### Conditional length and neighboring parts

| Frame | Added leading unknown coordinates | Raw fixed positions | Primary proposed positions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 254 slots | 180 | 0/127 | 25/127 |
| 256 slots | 182 | 0/128 | 25/128 |
| 258 slots | 184 | 0/129 | 25/129 |

The **entire first 127 plaintext positions have identical received-source
ownership** in these three frames. The longer two merely add one or two
wholly unobserved positions. The source cannot choose among them. The
254-slot frame is a representative of this equivalence, not a recovered
transmitted length. An independent check of the exact sparse 25-letter
pattern examined 106,953 placements across every even length 74–1000. Of
3,724 placements retaining at least fifteen observed halves, only these
three models at offset 13 fit without a change. This bounded compatibility
check excludes neither lower-support placements nor other loss patterns,
wording or longer frames.

A separately priced `VON` at 124–126 is compatible in the 254-slot model:
it retains two observed halves and supplies four missing coordinates.
Its `V` is wholly absent, and it is excluded from the primary output.
The proposed neighboring p129 A7 begins with the fully observed
`ALLGEMEINERHIERNICHTBEKANNTERPOLITISCHERLAGE`, which makes a connection through
“von” plausible. The [cross-page report assembly](#edition-cases-military-transylvania-situation-report)
remains conditional: the 5/6 November headings and receipt times conflict.
That context supplies no missing A6 coordinate. The earlier A5 repairs and
A7 printed-dash fill retain their separate costs.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p137-publicity-fragment-source-and-verification"></a>

### Source and verification

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — all 74 printed slots, preserving the three dashes:**

```text
DXXAF FVAAG FAVDA VVFAX VAXVV
---FV AAXGX VGGAV GXDGF XFAFG DAAGX FXVFA
GXXAF FVXGA XGVX
```

</details>

The original labels this `6TL` and prints `RICHI` without a length. The leading
`(interference)` annotation supports a loss hypothesis but supplies no count.
The source edition retains the three dashes at source positions 25–27 and
keeps the inferred leading loss separate from them.

The [experiment and exact certificates](../../experiments/p137_publicity_fragment/README.md)
provide the source crop, source-owner maps, forward-encryption witnesses,
letter-level repair costs, frame-equivalence proof and adverse semantic
alternatives. Discovery uses the already audited exact word/bigram dynamic
program; its optimum is exact only within that declared scoring model.
Full-length-family shuffled controls are diagnostic comparisons, not a
probability that the proposed text is correct. A fresh 127-letter control
ranked its true frame first among 264 lengths but recovered only 54 true
letters, directly demonstrating that fluent model wording can be wrong.
No independent native copy
of this clause or of `OEFFENTLICHKEIT` has been found in the searched corpus.

**Verification command — independent source and candidate checks:**

```sh
python experiments/p137_publicity_fragment/verify.py --verify
```

The historical source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX
Cipher System*, printed p137 / PDF p140. The period key and prior cryptanalysis
retain their attribution to George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno

## p137 B — Query whether the station is still staffed by its former personnel

**Edition context:** p137 B — Query about the station's former staff.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p137-station-staff-query-p137-b--query-about-the-stations-former-staff"></a>



**Recovery and source review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** A conditional
group-movement and three-loss reconstruction exposes a query about whether
the station is still staffed by its former personnel, followed by a request
to answer and the closing name Eilvese.

<a id="source-p137-b"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-p137-station-staff-query-p137-b"></a>

### p137 B

**Readable German — conditional 138-slot frame; three observed substitutions, two printed-mask fills and two inserted-slot fills; time unresolved:**

> Ist dortige Station noch vom alten Personal besetzt? Antwortet um `17?0`. Eilvese.

The question mark after *besetzt* is editorial punctuation. The question mark
inside `17?0` is one unresolved plaintext position, retained literally.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — primary conditional 138-slot frame, before substitutions and fills; 64/69 fixed positions:**

```text
ICTDORTIGEVTATIONN?CHVOMALT?NPERSONALBESETZTXANTWO?TETUM17?0XEILBES?X
```

</details>

The source prints **135 slots**, including two dashes, against `RIZI-138`.
The primary model moves the last printed group `VDF--` (source 130–134) to
retained-stream boundary 105, the beginning of the final printed row. It
then appends three unknown coordinates to reach the advertised length.
All 135 source slots remain represented once; none is excluded. The movement is part of the stated reconstruction.

For the fixed 69-position proposal, exact integer pricing compares **481,032
maps**: each of 27 printed groups, each of 131 destinations after removal,
and each of 136 boundaries for the three missing coordinates. The minimum
is three observed substitutions. Exactly **five maps** attain it: source
group 130 moves to boundary 103, 104, 105, 106 or 107, and all three missing
slots follow the resulting 135-slot stream. Every minimum gives 64/69 fixed
raw positions and the same 68/69-position edited proposal. The certificate
retains all five alternatives; boundary 105 is the primary display because
it coincides with a printed group and row boundary.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same primary frame; three observed substitutions, two printed-mask fills and two inserted-slot fills; 68/69 fixed positions:**

```text
ISTDORTIGESTATIONNOCHVOMALTENPERSONALBESETZTXANTWORTETUM17?0XEILVESEX
```

</details>

| Primary repair or frame operation | Exact account, zero-based indices |
|---|---|
| Source group movement | Source 130–134 to retained-stream boundary 105 |
| Missing coordinates | Three unknown slots appended at model 135–137 |
| Observed substitutions | Source 130 `V→F`, 131 `D→G`, 132 `F→X` |
| Existing printed-mask fills | Source 133 `-→A`, 134 `-→F` |
| Inserted-slot fills | Model 135 `?→V`, 137 `?→F` |

The three changes include all three observed coordinates of the moved group
in this primary layout; the movement does not conceal their price. The
other 130 observed coordinates remain unchanged. Each of the six possible

The independent [p127 personnel notice](127.md#edition-cases-radio-nov4-personnel-transmission-notice)
contains `HIER NOCH ALTES PERSONAL` and says transmission continues as
agreed. Its subject is compatible with this query. Its LP/NKJ route differs
from OSM/OUI here, and neither source explicitly identifies the other: this
is topical context, with no copied coordinates or proved reply relationship.

<a id="edition-cases-military-armistice-clause-witnesses-scope-and-sources"></a>

### Scope and sources

The p137 page heading says November 6 while both receiving timestamps
refer to November 5. These labels are preserved. The earlier source texts,
repairs and catalogue rows remain intact; this adds two physical witnesses,
not two new unique message bodies or a new decipherment of the period key.

| New physical record | Source slots | Raw fixed labels | Observed-coordinate substitutions | Source fills or geometry changes |

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys"></a>

## p137 D — Tell POT the OSKACHI key is no longer locally available

**Edition context:** Radio contact, operating times and an unavailable key.

**Related source pages:** [p100 C](100.md#source-p100-c), [p142 A](142.md#source-p142-a), [p150 A2](150.md#source-p150-a2).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-radio-contact-operating-times-and-an-unavailable-key"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

These four independent records describe a broken wire connection, timed
radio calls, an embassy receiving station and the local absence of an
`OSKACHI` key. They use unchanged previously published keys and complete
source frames. They are grouped by subject, not asserted to be one exchange.

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [collected intercepts](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [inputs](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/inputs.json) and
[certificates](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/certificates.json)
retain exact source rows, headers, key provenance, image hashes, raw readings
and all local repairs. Printed page numbers are three less than PDF page numbers.

<a id="source-p137-d"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-p137-d-the-oskachi-key-is-no-longer-here"></a>

### p137 D: the OSKACHI key is no longer here

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p137_D.png)
has `RIZI-102`. Its upper sender initial is overprinted, so the header is
conservatively retained as:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
D) ?CO V OSM (1.55 November 5th,)
RIZI-102
NF NRO V OSM
```

</details>

The page heading is November 6. Neither it nor the footer is used to resolve
the unclear upper callsign or the time's missing a.m./p.m. designation.
The two dots after the final cipher group `AX` are punctuation; the footer
is outside the 102-coordinate body.

All 51 raw plaintext positions are fixed under `Nov4-6`:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
POTSAGENDA3SSCHLUESSELOSKACHIHIERNICHTMEHRVORHANDEN
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate substitution, source **79: G→X**, changes the `3`
inside `DA3S` to `S`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
POTSAGENDASSSCHLUESSELOSKACHIHIERNICHTMEHRVORHANDEN
```

</details>

Readable German:

**Readable German:**

> POT sagen, dass Schlüssel OSKACHI hier nicht mehr vorhanden.

It asks that POT be told the `OSKACHI` key is no longer available here.
The key name itself is unchanged. The message does **not** say why it is
unavailable, identify a specific square or rank order, give its operating
period, or connect it to a separate challenge ciphertext. Its presence
inside a telegram decoded with `Nov4-6` does not make `OSKACHI` another name
for that transport key.

The raw numeral `3` remains visible in the original reading and numerical
ledger. Its local word repair does not reassign the square's digit `3`.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-verify-and-prior-credit"></a>

### Verify and prior credit

```sh
python experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/verify.py --verify
```

The independent standard-library verifier rebuilds every source witness,
checks raw domains and numerical fields, and prices substitutions separately
from source-dash fills. No source coordinate is inserted or removed and no
published square is changed. Re-encryption confirms this stated arithmetic,
not the unique history of a damaged word or the identities of station names.

The keys are prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno
Wacker**, [DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
also published in George Lasry's [2017-02-24 comment 4](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1).
Earlier unreviewed OCR-derived candidates existed. The bounded author-paper
check found no explicit examples of these bodies; it does not establish
universal first-decipherment priority.


<details>
<summary>Comparative source sections from other printed pages</summary>

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-p100-c-direct-contact-while-the-wire-is-broken"></a>

### p100 C: direct contact while the wire is broken

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p100_C.png)
is under a November 1 heading, with this November 2 reception line:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
C) UKS v ZÖN (2.03 a.m., November 2nd)
2235 (1) AN LP
RIZI-158
```

</details>

All 158 coordinates give 79 fixed plaintext labels under `Nov1-3`, without
any repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
WANNISTUNMITTELBARERVERKEHRMITEUCHXMUENCHENODERBRSLAUMEGLICHXDRAHTUNTERBROCHENX
```

</details>

The sender asks when direct communication with the recipient, Munich or
the place written `BRSLAU` will be possible, and says the wire connection
is interrupted. `BRSLAU` is naturally read as Breslau and `MEGLICH` as a
damaged spelling of *möglich*, but **both remain literal in the certificate**.
No missing plaintext letters are inserted. The separately printed
[p100 B](100.md#edition-cases-military-budapest-wire-break) gives a longer wire-break report;
this does not by itself prove a single transmission or a specific route.

This is distinct from the [p100 challenge](100.md#edition-cases-p100), whose earlier
Belgrade body remains credited to Armin.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-p142-a-0430-calling-signal-then-listen-again-at-0645"></a>

### p142 A: 0430 calling signal, then listen again at 0645

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p142_A.png)
is headed November 6:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) NKJ ZÖN v LP (08.25 p.m., November 6th)
FUER ZÖN 1900 (6/11)
RIZI-128
```

</details>

All 128 coordinates and 64 plaintext labels are fixed under `Nov4-6`, with
no substitutions or fills:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
GEBENSIEX0430X10XMINXVVVXDANNIHREFKSPRUNDHOERENSIEUNSWIEDERX0645
```

</details>

The instruction is to send **10 minutes of `VVV` at 0430**, then the
recipient's radiograms (`FKSPR`), and listen again at **0645**. All three
numerical fields are literal published-square readings. No extra day or
time zone is inferred from the evening reception time.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-p150-a2-receiving-station-in-the-embassy"></a>

### p150 A2: receiving station in the embassy

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p150_A2.png)
explicitly labels this **part 2**. Its first part has not been attached or
reconstructed in this edition:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) LP v NKJ (8.55 p.m., November 7th)
PERA OSMAINE 6/11
FUER EILKESE ZU SS D (5) 2200
2 TL RICHI-180
UMGEHEND WEITERGEBEN
```

</details>

The page heading is November 6. The literal `OSMAINE` and `EILKESE` spellings
and the November 7 reception remain unchanged. The instruction separator
before `UMGEHEND WEITERGEBEN` is outside the ciphertext.

The 180-slot source contains one dash and gives 89 fixed labels out of 90
under `Nov4-6`:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
JEDOCHHOERTEMPEGSSTMTXINBOTSCHAFTAUFEUCHXNAMEXQZXXADT?SSENCHIFFRITENXINMLLENPERIDENANRUFEN
```

</details>

Six known-coordinate substitutions and one dash fill give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
JEDOCHHOERTEMPFGSSTATXINBOTSCHAFTAUFEUCHXNAMEXQZXXADRESSENCHIFFRIRENXINALLENPERIDENANRUFEN
```

</details>

The receiving station (`EMPFGSSTAT`) in the embassy listens for the
recipient. The message supplies the literal name/separator field
`NAMEXQZXX`, asks for addresses to be enciphered, and says to call in every
period. **The precise name boundary within `QZXX` is left unresolved.**
`CHIFFRIREN` and `PERIDEN` remain literal spellings; no extra plaintext
letters are claimed. The opening `JEDOCH` is retained rather than inventing
the missing preceding clause.

Known-coordinate changes, all at zero-based source indices:
**23 X→V, 80 X→V, 86 F→A, 92 X→V, 150 A→V, 167 X→V**.
The separate printed-dash fill is **112 ?→A**. Two of those substitutions
jointly change one raw `E` to `F` in `EMPFGSSTAT`; the certificate does not
collapse their cost into a single coordinate repair.

</details>
